steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Key differences:

• Sugar: RNA uses ribose; DNA uses deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen).

• Bases: RNA has A, U, C, G; DNA has A, T, C, G (uracil replaces thymine).

• Strands: RNA is usually single-stranded; DNA is typically double-stranded, forming a helix.

• Stability: RNA is less chemically stable and degrades faster; DNA is more stable for long-term information storage.

• Function: RNA acts mainly in protein synthesis and regulation (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA, etc.); DNA stores the organism’s genetic blueprint.

• Location: In eukaryotes, DNA stays in the nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts); RNA is made in the nucleus and functions mostly in the cytoplasm.
